movzx eax, byte [rcx+off]; ret (or [rcx]).
mov byte [rcx+off], dl; ret (or [rcx]).
mov [rcx+off], 0; ret, byte to qword width. Same instruction form as the constant stores, with the constant 0.
mov [rcx+off], imm; ret with a non-zero constant, byte to qword width.
mov eax, [rcx+off]; ret (or [rcx]).

Calls 0x0016D6A0 with ecx = (pointer global non-zero), then returns a second global.

ret 0: returns at once.
rdx = [rcx+off]; when it and its word at +0x10 are non-zero returns that word plus the low 32 bits of rdx, sign-extended; otherwise 0.
Two mov [global], imm stores into two globals, then ret; byte to dword width.
Calls 0x002EF2B0 and returns one bit of a byte at a fixed offset in the returned block.
Calls 0x002EF2B0, clears one bit of a byte in the returned block, and sets it again when the argument is non-zero.
movss [global], xmm0; ret: stores the float argument into a global.
Loads a pointer global and returns one bit of a dword field of its object (shr, and 1).
Loads a pointer global and returns the qword at a fixed offset in what it points to.
Returns 1 when a pointer global is non-zero (cmp [global], 0; setne al).
lea rax, [global]; or rax, 1; ret: returns a static's address with bit 0x1 set.
Stores xmm1, xmm2 and xmm3 into three adjacent float fields of this.
Stores xmm1 and xmm2 into two adjacent float fields of this.
Divides the span [+0x60] - [+0x58] by 20 (multiply by 0x6666666666666667); when non-zero returns a float constant, else 0.0 when [+0x10] is 0, else the float at [[+0x18]+0x24].
mov ecx, imm; jmp target.

Stores 0 or 1 into a dword field of this, sets edx to a small constant, adds 0x20 (0x70 in four members) to rcx and jumps to one of four targets (0x00470050, 0x0046FFA0, 0x0051DDC0, 0x0051DBF0); the members come in 0 / 1 pairs.
mov rcx, [rcx]; jmp target: the offset-0 spelling of the member-pointer forwarder.
xor r9d, r9d; jmp target.
mov rcx, [global]; add rcx, off; jmp target.
Sets rdx = this, r8 = this+off, rcx = [this+0xE0] + off2 and r9 = the second argument, then jumps to 0x003A56C0.
add rcx, off; jmp target: calls a member sub-object's method.
mov rcx, [rcx+off]; jmp target: calls a method of a pointed-to member.
mov rcx, [rcx+off]; test rcx, rcx; jne target; ret.
mov rcx, [global]; test rcx, rcx; jne target; ret.
test rcx, rcx; jne target; ret: forwards only a non-null this.
rcx = rdx + ([this+0x48] - [[this+0x18]+0xF4]), edx = r8d, then jmp target.
The same relative address with the 64-bit r8 kept as rdx and r9d moved to r8d, then jmp target.
mov edx, imm; jmp target.
xor edx, edx; jmp target.
ecx = (ecx != 0), then jmp target.
lea rcx, [static]; jmp target: passes a static's address.
mov rcx, [global]; jmp target: passes a pointer global.
xor r8d, r8d; jmp target.

xor ecx, ecx; jmp target.
mov r8d, edx; xor edx, edx; jmp target: shifts the second argument to the third and passes 0 as the second.
Calls 0x002F2530(this); when it returns non-zero calls a second function on this; returns the first result.
Saves ecx != 0, calls a getter, then jmp target(result, saved bool).
Saves the low byte of ecx, calls a getter, then jmp target(result, saved byte).
Calls a function and returns al != 0 as 0 or 1.
Calls a function and returns eax == 0 as 0 or 1.
Saves ecx and edx, calls a getter, then jmp target(result, ecx, edx).
Calls a getter and returns the dword at a fixed offset in its result.
Calls a function with rcx = rdx and copies 24 bytes of its result to the pointer in r8.
Calls a function with rcx = rdx and copies fields +0x08 to +0x20 (qword, qword, dword, byte, dword) of its result to the record in r8.
Calls a getter, then jmp target with its result as rcx.
Saves ecx, calls a getter, then jmp target(result, saved ecx).
Saves rcx, calls a getter, then jmp target(result, saved rcx).
Calls one function and returns 0.
Calls one function, then jmp to another.
Calls 0x00263F10(rdx), a member function on that result, then jmp 0x0026B4E0(this, result).
ecx = imm, calls one function, then jmp to another.
Calls 0x0067F580(this) twice.
An exception-frame prologue ([rsp+0x20] = -2) around one call with the incoming arguments.
Calls one function on this, then three field-object functions on this+off with the saved edx, and returns the address of a later field.
Calls one function on this, then four field-object functions on this+off with the saved edx, and returns the address of a later field.
Calls 0x0036C1D0(3, 0xF), 0x0036A100(ecx), 0x0036C140(), and returns the middle call's result.
Calls a function with rcx = rdx and returns 1.
The same frame around one call with rdx = [this+0x18].
Calls 0x001FB840 with one string, then jmp 0x0020E630 with a second string and the saved ecx.
Saves four arguments, calls a getter, then calls a second function with the result and the four arguments (the fourth on the stack).
Saves three arguments, calls 0x00210B30, then jmp target(result, arg1, arg2, arg3).
Calls 0x00212CC0(this), stores edx at +0x18, installs a vtable and returns this.
Stores a constant (0 or 1) as the fifth argument and calls one function.
Calls one function on two member sub-objects of this, then jmp to another on this.
Calls one of two functions on rdx, chosen by the byte in r8b, and returns 1.
Calls 0x00267E10(r9) and jumps to one of two functions chosen by whether the result is zero.
Calls a predicate on this; when true calls a second function on this; then jumps to a third on this.
Saves ecx; calls a getter, and when non-null calls it again and jumps to target(result, saved ecx).
Saves rcx; calls a getter, and when non-null calls it again and jumps to target(result, saved rcx).
Returns 5 when bit 0x80000000 of r9d is set; otherwise sets it, calls a function on rdx + ([this+0x48] - [[this+0x18]+0xF4]) and returns 0.
When the pointer at this+off is non-null, calls a function on it and then clears the field.
When the byte at rdx+8 is non-zero, calls 0x005CDAA0(3, string); when the pointer at rdx+0x20 is non-null, calls 0x006108C0 on it; returns 1.
When one bit of the dword 0x01FD46D4 is clear, calls 0x00226BE0(imm, 0, 0, 0, -1, -1) and jumps to 0x00226280.
When one bit of the dword 0x01FD46D4 is set, calls 0x00225CD0(imm, -1) and jumps to 0x00226280.
Calls 0x00280120; when non-zero returns 0, else calls a function and returns eax == 0.
Calls 0x002F2D60(this); when non-zero calls a function on this, then 0x0044B960, stores its result in a field and returns 1.
Under a stack cookie: when a field of this is zero, builds a stack record, calls 0x00244F50, stores the result in that field and passes it to 0x00246AD0.
Calls 0x00280120; when zero calls 0x00267E10(r9) and jumps to a function with that result.

Resolves the argument with 0x003588B0, follows +0xC0 into the same 0x740-stride table, calls a function on the out record in rdx when +0x284 is set, zeroes its first 12 bytes when the handle or record pointer is missing, and always stores 1.0 at its +0xC.
Under a stack cookie: builds a stack record holding the sign-extended argument and calls 0x00244F50(imm, code address, record).
Calls a getter; when it returns non-null, calls it again and jumps to a second function with that result.
Saves the low byte of ecx; calls a getter, and when non-null calls it again and jumps to target(result, saved byte).
When this, the pointer at +0xC0 and its dword are valid (not null, not -1), jumps to a function with the record's word in ecx.
Calls 0x00426220(this, [rdx+8]); when it returns 0, jumps to a function on this.
Calls a predicate; when non-zero calls 0x00314D40(imm) and returns 1, else returns 0.
Calls 0x002F2D60(this); when non-zero calls a function on this and returns 1, else returns 0.
When bit 0x80000000 of r8d is clear, sets it and calls a function; returns 0.
The same resolution; when +0x284 is non-zero calls a function on the record and sets bit 0x800 of its +0x290.
Resolves the word at [[this+0xC0]] through the record table whose base is the qword 0x022C6F28 (stride 0x740) and jumps to a function when the record's dword +0x284 is non-zero.
Calls a predicate on rdx; when true calls a second function on rdx; always calls a third on rdx; returns 1.
When a pointer global is non-null, calls a function on it and then zeroes the global.
Frees the handle in a global through 0x003844F0 when it is non-null, then stores the sign-extended argument there.
Calls a float getter on rdx, passes the float to 0x00267F60(r9), then jumps to a function with the four original arguments.
Reads an integer from the record in r9 with 0x00267E10, passes it through one function and jumps to another with the result.
Reads three floats with 0x00267DB0 and an integer with 0x00267E10, calls 0x0016D6A0 and 0x003EB700 on the integer, then jumps to a function with the result and the three floats.
Reads three integers with 0x00267E10, passes the last through 0x00264010 and 0x00263F10, then jumps to a function with that result and the first two.
Calls 0x0026A1A0(rdx, 1), restores the four arguments and jumps to a function.
Calls 0x0026A1A0(rdx, 0), restores the four arguments and jumps to a function.
Calls 0x002640C0, reads an integer with 0x00267E10(r9), then jumps to a function with both.
When rdx is non-null writes a constant qword (a different one per member) and two zero qwords there; returns 1.
When rdx is non-null calls a function on it and installs a vtable at +0; returns 1.
When rdx is non-null writes three addresses at +0, +8, +0x10, zeroes +0x18 and +0x1C, and stores 1.0 at +0x20; returns 1.
When rdx is non-null calls a function on it and stores two addresses at +0 and +8; returns 1.
When rdx is non-null clears 0x90 bytes there with memset (0x00861EC0) and calls an initialiser on it; returns 1.

Advances the cursor in the fifth argument by 8, converts the double there to float, calls [this+8](rdx, float); when the third argument equals 0x006B0B20() with bit 0x1 set, stores the result at out+8, zeroes out+0 and returns 1, else 0.
Calls 0x0016D6A0 (ret 0) with a static's address and returns.
When a static container holds more than one byte and a non-null begin, returns the storage through slot 3 of its allocator object.
Clears a 0x50-byte static with memset, constructs its lock with 0x007DF6D0, and registers its teardown with atexit (0x00808B90).
When rdx is non-null calls a destructor on it; returns 1.
Deleting destructor: calls the destructor; when flag bit 0x1 is set frees this with 0x00584730, or, when bit 0x4 is also set, calls 0x0016D6A0(this, size); returns this.
The same deleting destructor with a vtable install before the destructor call.
Calls the base constructor on this, installs the derived vtable, returns this.
lea rax, [vtable]; mov [rcx], rax; ret.
The vtable-installing deleting destructor whose destructor call is always 0x00633390. Same instruction form as the previous family.
InitializeCriticalSection (IAT 0x008C20B0) on a static, then registers its teardown with atexit.
Calls 0x005DC6F0(static, string, 0), then registers its teardown with atexit.
Calls 0x005FDCB0 with a static's address, then registers its teardown with atexit.
When a pointer global is null, allocates a fixed size with 0x00210EC0, constructs the object in it, and stores the pointer.

Installs a vtable in a static; when a link static does not point at itself, calls slot 0x48 of the object in another static; calls 0x006B6700 on a member static; frees a buffer with 0x00584730 when bit 0x1 of a flag byte is set.
On rdx: when bit 0x80000000 is clear and the count is above 1, frees +8 with 0x00584730; zeroes both; returns 1.
When bit 0x80000000 of the count word at +0 is clear frees the pointer at +8 with 0x00584730; zeroes both.
On rdx: when bit 0x80000000 is clear calls a teardown with the pointer and the count; zeroes both; returns 1.
When the span [this] .. [this+0x10] holds more than one byte and begins non-null, calls slot 3 of the object at this+0x18.
When [this] is non-null, returns the span [this] .. [this+0x10] (masked to the element alignment) through slot 3 of the allocator object at this+0x18.
Calls two lookups on rdx; when the second is non-null calls the function at [this+8] with both results; returns 0.
Calls two functions on rdx; when the second is non-null calls [this+8] with rcx = result + [this+0x10]; returns 0.
Loads a handler global; when set, jumps to it with rdx = rcx and rcx = [r8+0x2E0].
mov rcx, [rcx+off]; mov rax, [rcx]; jmp [rax+slot].
Returns when rcx is null; otherwise jmp [[rcx]+slot].
mov rax, [rcx]; jmp [rax+slot]. Same instruction form as the fixed-slot adapters.
mov rax, [rcx]; jmp [rax+slot].

Initialises a record in this (zeroes +0 to +0x1B, +0x20 = rdx+0x38, +0x28 = the list's first node, +0x30 = a table address), steps it with 0x001B7CE0 until that returns true, then calls 0x001AA0A0; returns this.
For each index below the count at +0x18 (bit 0x80000000 masked, at least 1), calls 0x005CCB80(1) while a lookup's dword is positive.
Clears bit 0x2000 of the qword table[ecx]; when no bit but bit 0x1 remains, calls 0x00263FF0(ecx) and clears bit 0x8 of the byte at its +0x11; when a non-zero slot became zero, calls 0x0032F1B0(ecx).

Allocates 0x20 bytes through 0x0085E730 (malloc), constructs a record with edx, appends its pointer to the vector in this (end +8, capacity +0x10, grown by 0x001AB570), then jumps to 0x0018AFF0(0x0018B4E0(), record).
Walks the circular list at this+8 calling a predicate on each node's +0x10 with the three other arguments; returns 1 at the first true, else 0.
When ecx is within a bound, takes a row pointer from a table; when the row's first byte is non-zero returns its dword at +8 + edx*8, else -1.
Stores edx into entry ecx of a table (fixed stride); a negative index stores into entry 0, an index at or above the bound stores nothing.
Returns 0 when ecx is at or above a bound; otherwise takes row ecx (stride 0x294), wraps byte [row+1] + edx into 0 to 15, and returns the word at +0x4A of that 36-byte entry.
Walks a global chain (next at +8) comparing each node's name at +0 with the argument; returns the node or 0.
Recurses into [node], then calls slot 3 of the object at this+0x30 with (node, 0x38), moving to [node+8] until null.
The same recursive walk with node size 0x40, which also returns each node's own span [node+0x20] .. [node+0x30] through slot 3 of the allocator at node+0x38.
Returns 0x11 when the name at +8 is null; walks a global chain comparing names byte by byte; returns 0x12 on a match, else links this at the head and returns 0.
Walks a global chain (next at +0x10) comparing each node's name at +8 with the argument; returns the node or 0.
For every id of one class, 0x1000 * class + i below the class count, calls 0x003008A0(id, 0x63, 0, 1, 0).
Under a stack cookie: resolves a word id through the 0x740-stride table, checks each hop with 0x00426220, follows the record's +8 word the same way, and calls 0x0042EF90 for the words at +8 and +0xA.
Calls a getter with rcx = rdx and copies its fields from +8 onward to the record in r8, field by field.
Copies the vector at this+0x60 into a bank of float globals (adding each lane to a base), stores this in a global, then continues through 0x0039AF70, 0x00398F90 and others.
Under a stack cookie: copies a record with 0x00430B90 into this+0x110, publishes it to a bank of float globals, then runs a long sequence of fixed calls.
Two word globals select two 16-byte slots of a global record array; copies a 16-byte record and an 8-byte tail between them, advances the counters, and calls the function in rcx.
On rdx: when bit 0x80000000 of the count word at +0 is clear and the pointer at +8 is non-null, frees it with 0x00584730; zeroes both; returns 1 (59 bytes).
push rbx; sub rsp, 0x20; mov rcx, rdx; mov rbx, r8; call target; mov [rbx], rax; ...; ret (26 bytes): calls the target with the second argument and stores the returned pointer through the third.
